status_summary: On 2025-05-05 the Defense Secretary directed at least a 20 percent cut in four-star generals and admirals, at least 20 percent in National Guard general officers and 10 percent across all general and flag officers, with no timeline beyond acting quickly; 38 four-star officers were counted on 2025-03-31. The Army had said on 2025-05-01 that it would trim general officer positions without giving a number. In a State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico on 2026-09-30 the Secretary announced a further cut, bringing the total to 20 percent of roughly 800 general and flag officer positions (per AP and Air & Space Forces reporting), with completion by 2027-01-01 and no new written memo reported; how the cut is divided among the services was unclear. AP also said it was unclear whether the 2025 cuts had been completed, that Congress sets general officer numbers by law and positions can be left vacant by not sending nominations, and that more than two dozen senior military leaders have been fired or pushed into retirement since January 2025. The Mandate's wording is about limiting advancement and the count of senior officers; the actions combine billet cuts with removals, and Sen. Jack Reed, the ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, said eliminating senior positions must be done in consultation with Congress.
